facts.label: Pedir com educação
facts.sub: No balcão, use I’d like + item para pedir com educação e Can I get + item? para pedir algo a mais. Para tirar algo, diga No + item, please. Pergunta fixa: For here or to go?

facts.label: Monte o sanduíche
facts.sub: Nos delis dos EUA, você escolhe o pão, a carne, o queijo, os vegetais e o molho. As perguntas são rápidas, e as respostas também: “Whole wheat. Swiss. No onions.”

facts.label: Aqui ou para viagem
facts.sub: Essa pergunta aparece em quase todo balcão. For here quer dizer comer no local, e to go é para levar. O pedido é embalado de modo diferente.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: At a deli, you choose the bread, the meat and the cheese.
items.why: Most delis let you build the sandwich.

items.s: You must accept every vegetable the worker offers.
“For here or to go?” asks if you eat there or take it away.
items.why: It is the standard question at counters.

pages.title: Lunch at the deli · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday at noon in New Orleans. Ana is hungry, so she goes to a small deli near her office. The line is short, and the room smells like fresh bread. “**Next! What can I make for you?**” asks the man behind the counter.
“**I’d like a turkey sandwich, please,**” says Ana. “**What kind of bread?**” he asks. “Whole wheat, please.” “Cheese?” “Swiss cheese, please.” “Lettuce and tomato?” “Yes, but **no onions, please.**”

pages.title: Lunch at the deli · 2/3
paragraphs: The man puts the turkey on the bread. “**Mustard or mayo?**” he asks. “Just a little mustard,” says Ana. “**Anything else?**” “**Can I get a small soup, too?**” “Sure. Chicken or tomato?” “Tomato, please.”

“**For here or to go?**” the man asks. Ana looks at the small tables near the window. “**For here,**” she says. “I have an hour.” “That’s eleven dollars,” says the man. Ana pays with her card and takes a tray.

pages.title: Lunch at the deli · 3/3
paragraphs: She sits at a table and tries the sandwich. It is fresh, and the soup is hot. When she leaves, the man waves. “**Have a nice day!**” “**You too! Thanks!**” says Ana, and she smiles. Next Friday, she will come again and ask for the same sandwich.

pages.focus: o som “ch” de cheese e “sh” de fresh
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Em cheese o som é “tch”, e em fresh o final é “sh”. Muitos brasileiros trocam um pelo outro.
pages.how: Para cheese, junte a língua ao céu da boca e solte o ar de uma vez: “tchiz”. Em fresh, termine soltando ar contínuo: “fresh”.
pages.tip: Peça silêncio com “shhh” e note o ar contínuo. Para “tch”, o ar sai em um estouro curto.
